note: Route Condition ships one Condition plugin (id 'route', class Drupal\route_condition\Plugin\Condition\RouteCondition) that matches the active ROUTE NAME (analogue of core's request_path 'Pages' condition). Single config key 'routes' (textarea, one route name per line); '*' is a wildcard compiled to regex '.*'; a leading '~' excludes a route; input is lowercased; empty routes matches everywhere; first matching line wins; standard 'Negate the condition' also applies. There is no config UI of its own (configure=null), no services, no Drush, no permissions. On a placed block the config lives at block.block.<id> -> visibility.route.routes. Medium/hard cases place a system_powered_by_block in the olivero theme and read/write its visibility.route condition (config storage only; no theme regions rendering needed).

evals.prompt: In Drupal, I want a block to appear only on certain pages based on the route NAME (like 'entity.node.canonical'), not the URL path. The route_condition module provides this. What is the condition plugin id it adds, and what single configuration key holds the list of route names?
evals.expected_output: route_condition provides a Condition plugin with id 'route' (class RouteCondition). Its single config key is 'routes' — a textarea of one route name per line. On a block it is stored at block.block.<id> -> visibility.route.routes.

evals.prompt: Using the route_condition module's 'route' condition, how do I (a) match every entity's canonical view route with one line, and (b) exclude a single route? Describe the wildcard and exclusion syntax.
evals.expected_output: Use '*' as a wildcard (compiled to regex '.*'), e.g. 'entity.*.canonical' matches every entity canonical route. Prepend '~' (tilde) to a route name to exclude it, e.g. '~user.login'. One route per line; matching is case-insensitive; the first matching line wins.

evals.prompt: With the route_condition 'route' condition, what happens if I leave the routes field empty, and how does it read the current route? Does it match on the URL path or the route machine name?
evals.expected_output: An empty 'routes' value makes evaluate() return TRUE (matches everywhere). It reads the active route via the current_route_match service and matches on the route MACHINE NAME (e.g. entity.node.canonical), not the URL path — that is what distinguishes it from core's request_path 'Pages' condition.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site a block with id 'routecond_known' is placed in the olivero theme and uses the route_condition 'route' visibility condition to restrict where it shows. Inspect the live block configuration and state the exact route name it is restricted to.
evals.expected_output: block.block.routecond_known has visibility.route.routes = 'entity.user.canonical', so the block only shows on the user canonical (profile) route. Read it with: drush cget block.block.routecond_known visibility.route.routes

evals.prompt: A block with id 'routecond_neg' on this site uses the route_condition 'route' condition. Inspect its live visibility configuration and describe exactly which routes it targets, including any wildcard or exclusion it uses.
evals.expected_output: block.block.routecond_neg has visibility.route.routes with two lines: 'entity.node.*' (wildcard matching all node routes) and '~entity.node.edit_form' (tilde-excluding the node edit form route). So it targets node routes but not the node edit form.

evals.prompt: On this site a block with id 'routecond_task' is placed in the olivero theme but currently has an empty route_condition 'route' visibility (it shows everywhere). Using the route_condition module, configure that block's Route visibility condition so the block only appears on node canonical pages. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set block.block.routecond_task -> visibility.route.routes to 'entity.node.canonical' (or a wildcard that matches it, e.g. 'entity.node.*' or 'entity.*.canonical'), with negate false, and save. E.g. load the Block entity, set visibility route config, save.

evals.prompt: On this site a block 'routecond_excl' uses the route_condition 'route' visibility condition (currently matching only 'entity.node.canonical'). Using the route_condition tilde-exclusion syntax, add a rule so the block is additionally excluded from the user login route. Apply the change to the live block configuration.
evals.expected_output: Add a line '~user.login' to block.block.routecond_excl -> visibility.route.routes (the leading tilde excludes that route). The resulting value contains both 'entity.node.canonical' and '~user.login'.
